rawCandidates.title: REM dreaming relabels and persists memories from other workspaces and owners
rawCandidates.source: Recent active memory rows in one per-agent LanceDB table carry workspaceKey, scope, and ownerUserId and can belong to different workspaces/users.
rawCandidates.control: loadCandidateMemories receives the requested workspaceKey/agentId but filters only time/status/dream class; it neither compares row bindings nor calls checkAccess, and it preserves or defaults those bindings only after selection.
rawCandidates.sink: Foreign row text is sent to the pattern/narrative LLMs and copied into evidenceQuotes, patterns, trends, dream memories, dream echoes, and Markdown under the requested workspace identity.
rawCandidates.impact: A REM run for one workspace can disclose another workspace/user's memories to the configured model provider and persist exact evidence or derived content into artifacts visible and influential in the wrong workspace.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: A fake Lance query containing workspace-a and workspace-b rows returned both when workspace-a was requested. A full run with three workspace-b rows, force=true, and a workspace-a Neo store persisted one pattern labeled workspace-a whose evidenceQuotes were the three exact workspace-b confidential strings. The 14 related test files passed, but no REM mixed-workspace/owner assertion exists.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires a single agent table to contain rows for multiple workspace/user scopes and an enabled or authorized REM run targeting one of them. No control of the LLM is needed for exact pattern evidence persistence; narrative/echo disclosure quality depends on generation. Operational guidance prefers one agent per workspace for feature crons (README.md:221-224), but the schema and ACL model expressly support workspace/user distinctions inside an agent DB, and this REM command does not enforce that deployment assumption.

rawCandidates.title: Critical classifier processes and exports foreign-scope cards without object authorization
rawCandidates.source: Fresh unclassified memory rows can be workspace-scoped or scope:'user' with an ownerUserId while sharing an agent table.
rawCandidates.control: findRecentUnclassified receives only agent/time, filters no workspace/scope/owner, and runClassifier has no caller identity; updateCardType mutates the selected UUID without a record ACL check.
rawCandidates.sink: The full card enters the classifier model, its type is mutated, and critical content is returned as a pushMessages payload for the current cron carrier and serialized by the caller.
rawCandidates.impact: A private card can be disclosed to the wrong cron destination/provider and changed outside its owner/workspace authorization context.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: With a valid scope:'user', owner:'victim', workspace-b row, an agent-only run classified it as gesundheit, updated its type, and returned a push containing the full diagnosis string. test/memory-edit.test.js and critical-classifier tests passed but cover only time/type/error/rate behavior, not ctx or mixed ownership. The existing cand-critical-push-sensitive-log covers generic log disclosure; this candidate's independent root cause is cross-object selection and mutation.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires multiple owners/workspaces in one agent table and a classifier run. Classification/mutation occurs automatically; confidentiality impact additionally requires the cron carrier/log/provider to be visible outside the victim scope. A victim simply storing an unclassified critical memory supplies the trigger.

rawCandidates.title: Stale critical auto-accept confirms foreign user/workspace records
rawCandidates.source: Old unconfirmed critical rows include owner and workspace scope metadata in a shared per-agent table.
rawCandidates.control: findUnconfirmedCritical filters only cutoff/type/confirmed and autoAcceptStale passes only agent; markConfirmed updates by UUID with no ctx, owner, or workspace comparison.
rawCandidates.sink: The selected row's confirmed field is set to 1 by the daily background job.
rawCandidates.impact: A sensitive memory can be silently accepted under a different user's/workspace's job context, bypassing the owner review state and affecting later retention or confirmation workflows.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: A valid scope:'user' credential row owned by victim in workspace-b was returned to an agent-only auto-accept run and produced values:{confirmed:1}. The existing unit test verifies critical/cutoff selection and the mutation itself but supplies no owner/workspace mix (test/memory-edit.test.js:364-388).
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires an unconfirmed victim critical row older than 24 hours in an agent table containing more than one authorization scope. The scheduled job itself supplies execution; no UUID knowledge or direct command control is necessary. Security relevance depends on confirmed state having approval/retention consequences, which later validation should trace.

rawCandidates.title: Light dreaming strengthens semantically matched foreign-scope memories
rawCandidates.source: Conversation-derived insights drive a raw vector search that can return workspace- or user-scoped rows belonging to another principal in the same agent table.
rawCandidates.control: findActivatedMemories passes no ACL context or workspace filter to db.search, and lightDream forwards every non-dream hit UUID to strengthenMemory without checking entry.scope/owner/workspace.
rawCandidates.sink: strengthenMemory increments replayCount/lastReplayed in place; its compatibility fallback deletes and re-adds the complete foreign row.
rawCandidates.impact: One conversation can alter another user's memory dynamics and potentially its lifecycle/salience metadata, violating object-level integrity even though the foreign text is not directly returned.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: A workspace-a lightDream mock returned a valid scope:'user', owner:'victim', workspace-b hit from db.search; the run strengthened it and changed replayCount 2 to 3. light-dream data-loss and injection-guard tests passed, but no ACL/scope test covers activated-memory selection.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires a same-agent foreign memory semantically close to an attacker-controlled/session-derived insight and light dreaming enabled after the session. Top-five bounds limit breadth but do not authorize the selected object. Later validation should confirm whether replayCount/lastReplayed affect recall, decay, promotion, or only diagnostics.

rawCandidates.title: Workspace-wide dream echoes can surface one session's topic in another session
rawCandidates.source: Light dreams derive insights/narratives from one completed session, and REM dreams derive them from stored memories.
rawCandidates.control: The echo schema and workspace-wide file omit agent/session/chat/user/destination identity; loadFreshDreamEcho selects only by freshness, while the before-prompt hook knows the current context but supplies only workspaceDir.
rawCandidates.sink: The newest echo sentence is inserted into the next eligible prompt's fullMemoriesContext and can be reflected in the response to whichever session contacts that workspace first.
rawCandidates.impact: A confidential health, relationship, credential, or project topic from one chat can be alluded to or repeated to another user/session sharing the agent workspace.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: A temp-workspace validation appended 'victim-chat confidential health topic', then loaded and formatted it for a later hypothetical context; the text survived and the stored object had only sentence/topics/createdAt, with no identity field accepted by either API. tests/dream-echo.test.js passed escaping and bounding but contains no multi-session test.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: Requires two principals/sessions sharing workspaceDir, a generated echo from the victim, an allowed governor budget, and the other session being the next eligible contact before expiry/daily cooldown. The one-agent-per-workspace cron rule does not imply one chat/session per agent; final exploitability depends on actual binding topology and whether the answering model repeats the advisory echo.

rawCandidates.title: REM command info-logs the full generated dream narrative
rawCandidates.source: Up to 15 bounded snippets of stored memory text feed the default-enabled REM narrative generator, whose output can retain names, medical details, credentials, or other private content.
rawCandidates.control: Output is length-capped but not redacted; runRemDream assigns the whole narrative to report.narrative and the internal command serializes the complete report at info level.
rawCandidates.sink: api.logger.info receives JSON.stringify(result.report), including up to 3,000 narrative characters.
rawCandidates.impact: Service/plugin log readers can recover sensitive dream-derived memory content outside normal memory ACL and chat visibility controls.
rawCandidates.validationFacts: A no-write mock REM run placed a marker secret from memory material into a 72-character generated narrative; report.narrative and JSON.stringify(report) both retained the marker exactly. Code-level logging is complete. Validation must establish production logger persistence/access and representative model tendency to repeat versus abstract sensitive details.
rawCandidates.attackFacts: The narrative feature is enabled unless explicitly false. A stored sensitive memory plus an internal REM run is sufficient to create the log payload; no chat attacker is required. Confidentiality impact requires another principal/component with log access, and model behavior controls how much original detail appears.

notes: All five assigned paths were read in full at the immutable target. Six new candidates were retained for later validation, while cand-critical-push-sensitive-log and cand-mood-state-prompt-injection receive supporting evidence only. Prompt-data framing, fixed file suffixes, bounded outputs, and production forget/correct ACL wrappers suppress separate prompt-injection, traversal, resource-exhaustion, and raw delete/update candidates. No repository edits or feature changes were made.
